description.en-US: The code that was redeemed. Immutable: a redemption record answers 'which code was used on which order', and re-pointing it would rewrite history that a refund or an audit reads.

The order the code was applied to. Together with voucher_code_id this pair is unique, which is what enforces BR 26's one-use-per-order rule at the database rather than in a check that a concurrent request could race past.

Where this redemption stands. The four values are two pairs: 'reserved' becomes 'redeemed' when the order confirms or 'released' when the draft is cancelled or expires; 'redeemed' becomes 'reversed' when a return restores the use. The reserve/redeem split is the point of the table (BR 82) - a code applied to a draft must be held so a second customer cannot take the last use, and must be given back if that draft never becomes a sale.
When the code was applied to the draft order and its use was held.
When the order confirmed and the hold became a real use. Null while the redemption is still only reserved.

When the hold was given back without a sale - the draft was cancelled or expired. Distinct from reversed_at's meaning: a release says the code was never really used, a reversal says it was used and then returned. The two are told apart by status, and both are kept because a campaign report counts them differently.
When a return restored this use to the code (BR 32). Whether a return restores at all is the program's decision - restore_on_full_return and restore_on_partial_return - not this record's.
